newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey doctor charged in rat tail scheme.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey doctor charged in rat tail scheme.

text.p: A New Jersey doctor has been indicted for claiming he found a rat's tail in McDonald's french fries and "greasy particles" in a Coke after placing the substances there himself, prosecutors said on Thursday.

Michael Zanakis, 43, of Harding, New Jersey was named in a 23 count indictment charging him with mail and wire fraud and extortion. The indictment was brought by a federal jury in Eastern District of New York.

He was arrested by FBI agents on Thursday morning in East Orange, New Jersey. If convicted, he faces a possible prison term of five years on each of the 21 fraud counts and 20 years on each of the two extortion counts. Each count also carries a maximum fine of $250,000.

According to Zachary Carter, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, the first part of the scheme occurred in March 1993 when Zanakis told Coca-Cola Co. that he drank from a can of Coca-Cola Classic and ingested "small bits of greasy particles" causing nausea and gastritis.

Claiming he had to cancel patient evaluations and lost revenues due to the illness, he allegedly threatened to take his story to the media. He ultimately extorted $4,600 from Coca-Cola, prosecutors alleged.
The indictment charges that Zanakis himself placed the grease in the soda can and did not ingest any of it.

In another scheme that took place in January 1996, Zanakis bought a "Happy Meal" for his son at a McDonald's restaurant in Long Island and allegedly reported that he found a rat's tail in the french fries.

Claiming that his minor son had actually eaten a piece of the "fried rat tail," Zanakis allegedly threatened McDonald's Corp. Tri-Mac Management Inc., which owned the franchise at the restaurant and insurance carrier General Accident Insurance that if he was not paid $5 million, he would go public with the story.
He also allegedly threatened to put his son in front of a camera holding the rat's tail.
The indictment alleges that Zanakis got the rat tail before going to the restaurant, caused it to be fried and that he placed it in the package of french fries.
Zanakis had been an associate professor at the New York College of Osteopathic Medicine in Old Westbury, New York, at the time and had conducted studies and research using laboratory rats.
